messages.subject: Example data produced nonidentical results
parts:
Hi everyone,

I ran the example script using example data (Hawaiian Psychotria), but the results (Table 1) were a little bit different from those displayed under the example script (Table 2). For example, parameter d was 1.000000e-07 for model BAYARELIKE+J in Table 1, but it was actually 1.000000e-12 in Table 2. Could anyone explain why?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Example data produced nonidentical results
parts:
Hi,

I think those saved results in "Table 2" are very old, from the first generation of the example script in 2013 or so. Since then the packages used for Maximum Likelihood inference (optim, optimx, GenSA) have been updated, defaults may have changed, etc. And, I must have changed the default minimum limit of parameters "d", "e", etc. from 1e-12 to 1e-7.

All of these things could cause small differences in the ML results, although as you can see they are very close. For BAYAREALIKE, the worst-fitting model, you see a little variation in the ML estimate of d, this probably suggests the likelihood surface is very flat under that model (remember, the ML optimizers work by "climbing the hill" of the likelihood surface -- they use heuristics that are pretty good but not always perfect). It doesn't matter very much, though, because BAYAREALIKE has hundreds of times worst fit than the other models.

Cheers!
Nick
